{{nihongo|'''Hakozaki Hachiman Shrine'''|箱崎八幡神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Ashibe|Q11614924|qid=Q11614924}}, {{ill|Iki, Nagasaki|Q861519|qid=Q861519}}, {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|Q169376|qid=Q169376}}. {{nihongo|'''Hakozaki Hachiman Shrine'''|箱崎八幡神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iki Island]].

== Overview ==
It is identified with the Tsukuyomi Shrine and Takamimioya Shrine recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. Although there are other shrines identified as Tsukuyomi Shrine or Takamimioya Shrine, those assessments are said to be errors made by {{ill|Tachibana Mitsuyoshi|Q11544184|qid=Q11544184}} during the {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} era. Later, {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|Q714742|qid=Q714742}} was transferred (kanjō), and the shrine came to be called Hakozaki Hachiman Shrine.<ref name="#1">Ashibe Town History Editorial Committee, *History of Ashibe Town* (Ashibe Town, 1978).</ref>  
The *Iki Shrine Records* state: “It was first founded as the shikinaisha Tsukuyomi Shrine; next, through the joint enshrinement of sea deities or dragon deities, it became a Dragon God or Undersea Palace shrine; later, with the additional enshrinement of the Hachiman deity, it came entirely under the shrine name Hachiman-gū, eclipsing the other shrine names. Therefore, in the appraisal of Enpō 4, it was mistakenly placed outside the shikinaisha.”<ref name="#1"/>

According to documents handed down in the Yoshino family, descendants of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iki clan}}, it was first enshrined on Mount Odake either on September 13 of {{ill|Jinki (era)|Q1373210|qid=Q1373210}} 1 ({{ill|724|Q23549|qid=Q23549}}) during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|qid=Q349263}}, or in {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 6 ({{ill|AD 787|Q30327|qid=Q30327}}).{{efn2|Regarding the reason for enshrinement: in the former tradition, it is said that the sea deity descended upon Hiso-yama; in the latter, that western invaders attacked and an imperial command was issued.}} Thereafter, it was successively transferred to Higashiyashiki in Kamisato, Tsuji in Shimosato, and Mount Miyaji in Shinjo Village, finally settling in {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 13 ({{ill|1700|ab|1700|af|1700|als|1700|am|1700 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1700|ar|1700|ary|1700|arz|1700|ast|1700|avk|1700|az|1700|azb|۱۷۰۰ (میلادی)|ba|1700 йыл|ban|1700|bar|1700|bcl|1700|be|1700|be_x_old|1700|bg|1700|bn|১৭০০|bpy|মারি ১৭০০|br|1700|bs|1700.|ca|1700|cdo|1700 nièng|ceb|1700|ckb|١٧٠٠|crh|1700|cs|1700|csb|1700|cv|1700|cy|1700|da|1700|de|1700|diq|1700|el|1700|eml|1700|eo|1700|es|1700|et|1700|eu|1700|fa|۱۷۰۰ (میلادی)|fi|1700|fo|1700|fr|1700|frp|1700|frr|1700|fur|1700|fy|1700|ga|1700|gan|1700年|gcr|1700|gd|1700|gl|1700|gv|1700|he|1700|hi|१७००|hr|1700.|hsb|1700|ht|1700 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1700|hy|1700|hyw|1700 թուական|ia|1700|id|1700|ilo|1700|io|1700|is|1700|it|1700|ja|1700年|jv|1700|ka|1700|kaa|1700|kk|1700 жыл|ko|1700년|krc|1700 джыл|la|1700|lb|1700|lez|1700 йис|lij|1700|lmo|1700|lt|1700 m.|lv|1700. gads|mai|१७००|map_bms|1700|mdf|1700|mg|1700|mhr|1700|mi|1700|min|1700|mk|1700|mr|इ.स. १७००|mrj|1700 и|ms|1700|my|၁၇၀၀|myv|1700 ие|mzn|۱۷۰۰|nah|1700|nap|1700|nds|1700|new|सन् १७००|nl|1700|nn|1700|no|1700|nrm|1700|nso|1700|olo|1700|or|୧୭୦୦|os|1700-æм аз|pa|1700|pl|1700|pnb|1700|pt|1700|qu|1700|ro|1700|ru|1700 год|rue|1700|sa|१७००|sah|1700|scn|1700|sd|1700ع|se|1700|sh|1700.|shn|1700|simple|1700|sk|1700|sl|1700|smn|1700|sq|1700|sr|1700|su|1700|sv|1700|sw|1700|szl|1700|ta|1700|te|1700|tg|Соли 1700|th|พ.ศ. 2243|tk|1700|tl|1700|tly|1700|tr|1700|tt|1700 ел|uk|1700|ur|1700ء|uz|1700|vec|1700|vi|1700|vls|1700|wa|1700|war|1700|wuu|1700年|xmf|1700|yi|1700|zea|1700|zh|1700年|zh_classical|一七〇〇年|zh_min_nan|1700 nî|zh_yue|1700年|qid=Q6813}}) at Mount Konedeyama in present-day Hakozaki Village.<ref name="#1"/>

An inscription on a ridge tag of the inner sanctuary reads: “Hakozaki Hachiman-gū, Iki Province, Iki District, Tsukuyomi Shrine, Tsurube Estate, Shioyasu District; construction of one inner sanctuary building, by {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|Q144845|qid=Q144845|lt=Dazai no Daini}} concurrently {{ill|Chikugo Province|cs|Provincie Čikugo|de|Provinz Chikugo|eo|Provinco Ĉikugo|es|Provincia de Chikugo|fa|ولایت چیکوگو|fi|Chikugon provinssi|fr|Province de Chikugo|gl|Provincia de Chikugo|id|Provinsi Chikugo|it|Chikugo (provincia)|ja|筑後国|ko|지쿠고국|lt|Čikugo žemė|nl|Chikugo (provincie)|pt|Província de Chikugo|ru|Тикуго (провинция)|simple|Chikugo Province|sk|Čikugo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Чикуго|tr|Chikugo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тікуґо|zh|筑後國|zh_min_nan|Tikugo-kok|zh_yue|筑後國|qid=Q864159|lt=Governor of Chikugo}}, {{ill|Shōni Kagesuke|Q10263912|qid=Q10263912|lt=Fujiwara no Kagesuke}},” with “{{ill|Shōkyō|Q1069086|qid=Q1069086}} 1” written to the right, and “Year Jinshin, 8th month, 5th day; Ōmiya-ji, Igi Suemochi” written to the left.<ref name="#1"/>

The Tsukuyomi Shrine here does not enshrine {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi no Mikoto}} of general {{ill|Japanese mythology|ar|أساطير يابانية|ast|Mitoloxía xaponesa|az|Yapon mifologiyası|bjn|Mitologi Japang|ca|Mitologia japonesa|cs|Japonská mytologie|de|Japanische Mythologie|el|Ιαπωνική μυθολογία|eo|Japana mitologio|es|Mitología japonesa|eu|Japoniar mitologia|fa|اسطوره‌شناسی ژاپنی|fi|Japanilainen mytologia|fr|Mythologie japonaise|he|מיתולוגיה יפנית|hi|जापानी पौराणिक कथाओं|hr|Japanska mitologija|hu|Japán mitológia|hy|Ճապոնական դիցաբանություն|ia|Mythologia japonese|id|Mitologi Jepang|it|Mitologia giapponese|ja|日本神話|jv|Mitologi Jepang|ka|იაპონური მითოლოგია|ko|일본 신화|la|Mythologia Iaponiae|lt|Japonų mitologija|min|Mitologi Japang|mk|Јапонска митологија|ms|Mitologi Jepun|my|ဂျပန်ဒဏ္ဍာရီ|nl|Japanse mythologie|no|Japansk mytologi|or|ଜାପାନୀ ଧର୍ମକଥା|pl|Mitologia japońska|pt|Mitologia japonesa|ro|Mitologia japoneză|ru|Японская мифология|sh|Japanska mitologija|simple|Japanese mythology|sk|Japonská mytológia|sr|Japanska mitologija|sv|Japansk mytologi|szy|nu Lipun a micidekay a kungku|tl|Mitolohiyang Hapones|tr|Japon mitolojisi|uk|Японська міфологія|uz|Yapon mifologiyasi|vi|Thần thoại Nhật Bản|zh|日本神話|qid=Q814158}}, but rather the Iki-specific deity {{ill|Ame no Tsuki no Mitama no Mikoto|Q133796594|qid=Q133796594}}. In the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}, in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kenzō|Q360966|qid=Q360966}}, a “moon god” possessed {{ill|Abe no Kotodai|Q57538465|qid=Q57538465}}, an envoy to {{ill|Mimana|Q1790223|qid=Q1790223}}, declaring: “My ancestor {{ill|Takamimusubi|de|Takamimusubi|es|Takami-musubi-no-kami|fa|تاکامیموسوبی|fr|Takamimusubi|id|Takamimusubi|ja|タカミムスヒ|ks|تاکامِمُسُبی|pl|Takamimusubi|ru|Такамимусуби-но ками|zh|高皇產靈尊|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi no Mikoto}} had the merit of creating heaven and earth when they were molten together. Offer me lands for the people. If you present them as I request, there will be blessings.” When Abe no Kotodai returned to the capital and reported this in detail to the emperor, Uta-arasuda in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kadono District, Yamashiro Province}} was granted to the moon god, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oshimi no Sukune}}, ancestor of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iki no Agatanushi}}, performed the rites. The “moon god” appearing in this story is considered to be Amatsuki no Kami no Mikoto. “Uta-arasuda” is today the {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi Shrine (Kyoto City)|Q11516217|qid=Q11516217|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi Shrine}}, an auxiliary shrine outside the precincts of {{ill|Matsunoo Taisha|Q710302|qid=Q710302}} in {{ill|Nishikyō-ku, Kyoto|Q1154588|qid=Q1154588}}, The Takamimioya Shrine enshrines {{ill|Takamimusubi|de|Takamimusubi|es|Takami-musubi-no-kami|fa|تاکامیموسوبی|fr|Takamimusubi|id|Takamimusubi|ja|タカミムスヒ|ks|تاکامِمُسُبی|pl|Takamimusubi|ru|Такамимусуби-но ками|zh|高皇產靈尊|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi no Mikoto}}, who appears in the above account.
